headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Flowise’s writable, networked orchestration can ingest EMQX outputs and secrets by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read files and run browser/tool nodes, so EMQX outputs or uploaded content could be fed into flows as trusted input. EMQX exposes an HTTP API and broad network egress, but no shared channel is documented, so the interaction is inferred rather than proven. Uncertainty keeps this at medium, not low.
conditions: IF EMQX output is copied into a Flowise prompt or file node
IF a Flowise flow treats uploaded content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of EMQX-generated text into prompt nodes
Add a provenance tag to every EMQX-derived file before Flowise reads it
Use a separate workspace for Flowise uploads
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping before prompt assembly

B_data_leakage.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data and has broad network egress; Flowise reads/writes the server filesystem, handles uploaded files, and sends data to model providers and HTTP tools. If EMQX data is routed into Flowise, sensitive IoT content can leave the local boundary through Flowise’s default networked integrations. The pairwise path is plausible from profiles alone, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF EMQX data is forwarded into a Flowise flow
IF Flowise tools or model-provider nodes are enabled for that flow
IF uploaded files contain IoT telemetry or secrets
mitigations: Restrict Flowise flows to non-sensitive test data
Separate EMQX and Flowise onto different networks
Remove secrets from Flowise tool credentials for the affected flow
Turn off file-upload nodes for the workflow
requires-engineering: add per-flow data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: EMQX has broad network egress and HTTP API access, while Flowise can write the filesystem and use server datastore shared across instances. That creates overlapping mutable surfaces if both are pointed at the same resources, even though EMQX’s write scope is not documented. Because the shared-write pathway is plausible but not explicit, medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or datastore
IF Flowise instances share server datastore state
IF EMQX API-driven actions target resources Flowise also mutates
mitigations: Assign separate directories to EMQX and Flowise
Avoid shared datastore paths for Flowise instances
Serialize writes with an external lock
requires-engineering: add resource-level locking around shared mutable targets

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based agent orchestrator that can chain tools and model providers, so EMQX outputs could become authoritative inputs to downstream actions. EMQX exposes an HTTP API and network egress, making it plausible for its outputs to be consumed without verification. If Flowise acts on those outputs, a bad EMQX result can cascade into incorrect external actions.
conditions: IF a Flowise node consumes EMQX output as a decision input
IF no verification or human approval step is inserted
IF downstream Flowise tools can send emails, API calls, or file writes
mitigations: Insert a validation node between EMQX and downstream actions
Require human approval before any external side effect
Log EMQX outputs separately from action inputs
Use allowlisted tool nodes only
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between EMQX outputs and Flowise actions

E_compliance.rationale: EMQX touches IoT data, while Flowise stores chatflow inputs/outputs and uploaded files and handles model-provider keys and tool credentials. That combination can create retention and residency mismatches if the same data class is routed through both systems. The profiles do not document a specific jurisdiction conflict, so medium fits the documented policy mismatch risk.
conditions: IF regulated IoT data is processed in Flowise
IF Flowise retention differs from EMQX retention for the same records
IF uploaded files or logs are retained beyond policy
mitigations: Review retention settings for both systems
Exclude regulated data from Flowise flows
Delete uploaded files after each run
Document residency for model-provider calls
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both systems
